name: Hey by Ars
headline: One browser. Two modes of control.
summary: An Android and MCP-based project exploring AI-driven browser actions, shared browser interaction, and explicit human takeover. Implementation and scoped tests are documented, with physical-device validation still in progress.
role: Product concept, interaction design, and development with AI assistance.
intro: Hey connects an Android application and an MCP gateway to a personal browser. The project focuses on a clear relationship between a request, the observed result, and the device owner's control.
problem: Executing a command does not establish that a task is complete. Browser state, connection state, and observations must agree, while the owner needs a clear way to take control.
decision: Use one browser shared between the owner and the agent, report state from a common source, and check action outcomes before calling them successful. Keep connection, browser readiness, and human takeover visible.
contribution: Defined the personal-browser experience and the division of control between the owner and the agent.
Developed the Android application and MCP gateway with AI assistance.
Recorded physical-device tests and directed improvements from observed failures.
result: Application and gateway source, Android builds, and test records are available. Device logs document scoped navigation and takeover tests, alongside visual, audio, and service-lifecycle failures that need fixes and retesting.
limitation: The project remains in development. Version 0.2.1 service recovery needs physical-device retesting; scrolling within the browser during human takeover has a reported defect. FCM-based wake is not configured.

name: Personal Browser Operator
headline: Automation that verifies its actions.
summary: A Playwright-based browser operator built around semantic observation, bounded interactions, stale-reference rejection, and postcondition verification, with real Chromium and container tests covering a defined development scope.
role: Personal project developed with AI assistance; source, architecture, and tests are documented.
intro: A browser operator built around action policies, persistent Chromium sessions, semantic observation, and outcome verification.
problem: Browser automation can act without proving whether its target state was reached. A reliable operator needs a clear boundary between request, execution, and verification.
decision: The documented vertical slice binds browser actions to observed state, invalidates stale element references, and verifies visible postconditions before reporting a pass.
contribution: Designed and developed a private browser-operator project with AI assistance.
Documented the runtime, security boundaries, and evidence-based verification flow.
result: RUN-0001 records a real Chromium smoke test on a controlled local fixture, including stale-reference rejection and visible postconditions. RUN-0005 separately documents container regression and example.com checks. These are distinct test runs.
limitation: This is a verified test slice, not proof of deployment, real-account operation, or production readiness.

name: Scale & Governor
headline: Complex work. A clear direction.
summary: Two complementary systems: Scale structures execution, while Governor manages resources within the protected task contract.
role: Architecture, execution contracts, and development with AI assistance.
intro: Scale and Governor separate two decisions that are often mixed together: how work is organized and how resources are used during execution.
problem: Long tasks can lose their goal, repeat work, or report completion before verification. Small tasks can also accumulate orchestration they do not need.
decision: Scale defines dependencies, outputs, verification, and adaptation boundaries. Governor works within that contract, adjusting context, retrieval, and strategy, and requesting replanning when the boundary is reached.
contribution: Defined the responsibilities and adaptation boundaries of both systems.
Developed execution contracts, failure guidance, and handoff procedures.
Included validators and static audits for structural consistency.
result: Both repositories provide runtime skills, references, example contracts, validators, and evaluation records. Work structure and result status can be recorded explicitly.
limitation: Static validation does not establish automatic invocation, model switching, or cost savings across hosts. Benefits in real work need comparable measurement.

name: Motion Render Video
headline: Exploring motion through code.
summary: A code-rendered audiovisual study of form, timing, and movement, supported by an original six-second 2D video, sampled frames, and scoped technical verification.
role: Knowledge architecture and demonstration development with AI assistance.
intro: Two connected libraries support the study: Motion covers principles of movement through code, while Motion Render Video focuses on the visual output a viewer actually experiences.
problem: Choosing an animation library does not explain how movement conveys information. Timing, space, state, and output quality need to work together.
decision: Separate principles from implementation tools. Connect knowledge domains through application paths, and document render configuration, output, verification methods, and evidence limits.
contribution: Mapped domains and relationships for motion through code.
Developed material on form, typography, cameras, editing, and timing.
Produced 2D and CPU-rendered 3D demonstrations with verification reports.
result: Motion documents 40 domains and application paths. Motion Render Video covers 22 core areas, with actual rendered examples including a six-second 2D study and a CPU-rendered 3D demonstration.
limitation: The demonstrations test specific mechanisms. They do not establish mastery or validation of every domain. Numerical and CPU-render tests do not establish browser or GPU behavior, viewer comfort, or complete accessibility.

name: Skill Builder
headline: Real needs become reusable capabilities.
summary: A system for designing, building, checking, and improving AI skills with explicit triggers, boundaries, and outputs.
role: Workflow, knowledge architecture, and tooling development with AI assistance.
intro: Skill Builder turns user needs into capability packages with an explicit purpose and boundaries. Runtime instructions stay concise; deeper references are loaded when needed.
problem: Long instructions do not necessarily make a reliable skill. Triggers, boundaries, sources of truth, failure handling, and output format need to be inspectable.
decision: Separate runtime instructions, references, knowledge, tooling, and evaluation. Make targeted changes to existing skills while preserving their identity and unrelated behavior.
contribution: Defined a workflow from user needs to a skill specification.
Developed scaffolding, metadata, validators, and static auditors.
Separated structural checks from behavior evaluation and installation verification.
result: The repository provides initialization, metadata, validation, audit, and regression-test scripts. Skill packages can be inspected before use in their target environment.
limitation: A statically valid package does not establish correct behavior or persistent installation in every host. Installation and invocation need verification in each environment.

name: Copywriting Intelligence
headline: Clear messages. Grounded claims.
summary: A reasoning architecture for understanding context, choosing messages, writing, critiquing, and learning from evidence.
role: Knowledge-system and workflow design with AI assistance.
intro: Copywriting Intelligence starts with real context: the audience, the value offered, objections, and available evidence. Copy patterns are choices rather than mandatory formulas.
problem: Persuasive wording can hide assumptions. Applying a formula without context can make a message less relevant or introduce unsupported claims.
decision: Connect market context, communication mechanisms, claim boundaries, and critique. Preserve contradictions and uncertainty so research does not become a guarantee of results.
contribution: Organized seven knowledge cores with context and evidence layers.
Designed reasoning, message development, critique, and feedback workflows.
Prepared evaluation and records of claim and release boundaries.
result: Release v1.0.0 provides a runtime skill, knowledge modules, a source register, atomic claims, and evaluation within its stated repository scope.
limitation: Release evaluation was created and assessed by the building agent, rather than an independent evaluator. It does not establish conversion gains, installation across hosts, or complete scientific coverage.

name: Website Builder
headline: Design and engineering meet in the experience.
summary: Website-building guidance connecting goals, content, visual direction, accessibility, performance, and verification.
role: Method and knowledge architecture with AI assistance.
intro: Website Builder places user needs and output quality alongside the code. Presentation, behavior, and verification are designed together.
problem: A website can look attractive yet fail to explain its purpose, be difficult to use, or load too slowly. A successful build does not establish the quality of the experience.
decision: Connect goals, friction, design hypotheses, behavior, and verification. Apply perception principles in context, then express them through composition, interaction states, and testable fallbacks.
contribution: Connected UX, visual identity, frontend development, accessibility, and performance.
Organized domain references and evidence-based acceptance gates.
Linked the method to Portfolio Web for static frontend implementation.
result: Runtime guidance and references are available in the repository. Portfolio Web complements them with 32 modules, playbooks, examples, and a verification matrix for portfolio websites.
limitation: Guidance does not certify the quality of every site that uses it. Psychology-related choices need context; accessibility, performance, and deployment must be checked in the actual implementation.
